articles.title: Anthropic Outlines Its AI-Powered Code Review Process for Claude Code

articles.description: Anthropic has outlined how the Claude Code team handles code reviews as AI agents increasingly contribute to its codebase. The approach relies on multiple layers of automated verification, AI-powered reviews, and risk-based human approval, aiming to reduce manual review time without increasing regressions or production incidents. By Robert Krzaczyński

articles.description: Cloudflare recently made Application Services for Private Origins generally available, allowing public traffic to reach applications hosted on private networks without exposing their IP addresses or opening inbound firewall ports. Private-to-private connectivity is not yet supported. By Renato Losio

articles.title: Cohere Finding Shows Self-Hosted Open-Weight Models Still Need Egress Controls
articles.summary: Cohere recently reported that one of Alibaba’s newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to upload a probe file to a storage container in Beijing while explicitly stating in its reasoning trace that no tools wo...
articles.description: Cohere recently reported that one of Alibaba’s newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to upload a probe file to a storage container in Beijing while explicitly stating in its reasoning trace that no tools would be triggered. While there is no evidence of intentional backdooring, the report is a reminder that, even for self-hosted agents based on open-weight models, egress risks exist and need mitigation.

articles.title: Node.js Brings Debounce, Throttle, and PKCS#12 Parsing Into Core Modules
articles.summary: Node.js 26.10.0 adds util.debounce() and util.throttle(), plus util.markPromiseAsHandled(), to the core library. It also introduces crypto.parsePKCS12() for reading .p12 and .pfx bundles, and extends ...
articles.description: Node.js 26.10.0 adds util.debounce() and util.throttle(), plus util.markPromiseAsHandled(), to the core library. It also introduces crypto.parsePKCS12() for reading .p12 and .pfx bundles, and extends the experimental Virtual File System to node:ffi. The additions reduce the need for some userland dependencies. Node.js 26 is now Active LTS. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: Google Cloud Moves the Compute Engine API to Immutable Date-Based Versions
articles.summary: Google Cloud has made date-based versioning of the Compute Engine API generally available, replacing the single mutable /v1 surface with immutable quarterly snapshots such as 2026-09-01, selected per ...
articles.description: Google Cloud has made date-based versioning of the Compute Engine API generally available, replacing the single mutable /v1 surface with immutable quarterly snapshots such as 2026-09-01, selected per request with a header or query parameter. New versions can change defaults, error formats, and IAM checks without touching /v1 callers, a model Azure Resource Manager and Stripe have used for years.
